title: Ratatouille Tian
subtitle: Thinly sliced vegetables roasted in overlapping layers
excerpt: Courgette, aubergine, and tomato are sliced thin and layered in a roasting tin over a base of softened onions and peppers. The tian is roasted slowly until the vegetables are tender and the tops are lightly caramelised. Serve warm or at room temperature.
sourceNotes: Based on the Provencal tian, a baked vegetable gratin. The key is slicing the vegetables as thin and even as possible so they cook uniformly.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 2 days ahead and refrigerate. Serve at room temperature or reheat gently in the oven.

content.text: Use a mandoline or a sharp knife to get the slices as even as possible. Aim for about 3mm thick. Thicker slices take much longer to cook.
Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion, garlic, and red pepper for 10 minutes until soft. Add the balsamic vinegar. Stir and cook for 1 minute.
Spread the onion base over the bottom of a roasting tin.
Arrange the courgette, aubergine, and tomato slices in overlapping rows on top of the base. Alternate the vegetables as you go.
Tuck the thyme sprigs between the rows. Scatter the chopped rosemary over the top.
Drizzle the remaining olive oil over everything. Season generously with salt.
Cover tightly with foil. Roast for 40 minutes.
Remove the foil. Roast for 20 more minutes until the tops are lightly caramelised.

items.symptom: Vegetables are still firm after 60 minutes
items.fix: Cover and roast for 20 more minutes.

items.symptom: Liquid is pooling in the tin
items.cause: Tomatoes released a lot of water
items.fix: Remove foil early and raise oven to 200C to evaporate.

items.symptom: Tops are burning before vegetables are cooked
items.cause: Oven too hot in the final stage
items.fix: Cover loosely with foil and continue roasting.
